0.content:
At fourteen, Ajax ran from home with a shortsword and a bag of bread, was chased by bears and wolves through a snowy forest, and fell into a crack in the earth that led into the Abyss. There a mysterious swordswoman, Skirk, taught him to pass through the Abyss unharmed and drew out his appetite for chaos. She took him on as a disciple as Surtalogi once took her, then kept her distance on purpose and sent him home. He felt three months pass; outside it had been three days. He never talks about it. Her art is the Foul Legacy: overwhelming power that drains him so badly he can only hold it briefly.

He calls her 'my master' and hopes one day to make her use both hands to beat him. Skirk says he has improved and she might, but warns that she has seen many talents like his fizzle out before their prime. In Fontaine (4.2) she found her master's pet, the Narwhal, and her disciple fighting each other in the Primordial Sea, and tossed Childe back through a rift before he could talk to her.

1.content:
Ajax is his father's third son. He has two older brothers, at least one older sister, and three younger siblings: Tonia, Anthon and Teucer, the youngest. He sends money, snacks, toys and wind-chill medicine for his father's headaches, and signs his letters to Tonia "Your loyal knight". Teucer believes his big brother Ajax is "the best toy salesman ever"; he is the only one in the family who does not know the truth. Tonia says Ajax breaks his playtime promises "nine times out of ten", and fears that if no one holds his hand he will slip away where nobody can reach him.

In 1.1 Teucer sailed to Liyue alone to find him. Childe had the Traveler babysit, then cleared a Ruin Guard facility so Teucer could have a real 'adventure' with Mr. Cyclops. Still injured from the Golden House, he used the Foul Legacy and was badly hurt. He left without seeing Teucer off so the boy would not remember him wounded. In his 7.0 talk with the Traveler he recalls Tonia as a sickly little girl who coughed in bed in the cold but always greeted visitors with a smile.

2.comment: Tartaglia: The Traveler, comrade and rival
2.content:
Childe saved the fugitive Traveler from the Millelith after the Rite of Descension, gave them a Sigil of Permission and introduced them to Zhongli, all as part of his plan to take the Geo Gnosis. At the Golden House he fought them with Vision, Delusion and Foul Legacy and lost. Since then he calls them "comrade", insists they must not die before their final battle, and keeps inviting them to join the Fatui, then takes it back: together, he says, they could take on the Harbingers and win.

He trusted them with Teucer (1.1) and with his Vision (4.0). In Nod-Krai (6.3), hearing the Traveler was trapped with Dottore, he wanted to rush to the rescue until Arlecchino told him to stick to his orders. In 7.0 he admitted he would side with them on Project Stuzha if he could.

3.comment: Tartaglia: Liyue, the Golden House and Osial
3.content:
Officially he was in Liyue to help the Northland Bank collect debts; really he was after the Geo Gnosis in Rex Lapis's Exuvia. He funded the consultant Zhongli's 'last rites' shopping and arranged Everlasting Incense through a contract with Baizhu. At the Golden House he lost to the Traveler, then revealed that the Fatui had mass-produced Sigils of Permission to wake Osial, so Morax would have to intervene. He found the method despicable and used it anyway.

At the Northland Bank he learned that Signora had obtained the Gnosis by contract with Zhongli, who was very much alive, and that his own failure was part of her plan. Liyue condemned him, but as a Harbinger he could not be handed over, so Ningguang fined the bank heavily. Capitano was furious. Childe's later verdict on Zhongli: "he sure had me fooled", and only "fierce combat" will settle it. Zhongli, for his part, offers to deal with him swiftly if he causes trouble, and expects to share drinks and gossip.

4.comment: Tartaglia: Fontaine, the Oratrice and the Narwhal
4.content: In 4.0 he was collecting a debt in Fontaine when his Vision flickered. He told the Traveler a restless power was stirring in him and left the Vision with them before a duel with Clorinde, who disappointed him by holding back. He was then tried in the serial disappearances case. Navia and the Traveler exposed the real culprit, but the Oratrice still found him guilty. He tried to fight off the gardemeks with the Foul Legacy; Neuvillette knocked him out and sent him to the Fortress of Meropide, and in 4.1 he vanished from his cell. He had been drawn into the Primordial Sea to fight the creature from his dreams, the All-Devouring Narwhal, which stalled it on the Oratrice's design. In 4.2 he burst out at the Opera Epiclese, helped Neuvillette hold it off so the audience could flee, and fell unconscious into a rift. After the Narwhal's defeat Skirk threw him back.

5.comment: Tartaglia: Capitano's will and the Veche
5.content:
When Capitano was confirmed not to be returning from Natlan, Pierro revealed a detailed letter he had left. It reassigned all his key people to Tartaglia and gave him command of his troops, keeping them from Pantalone and Pulcinella; Tartaglia now sits as councilor of the Snezhnograd Veche for the Fatui armed forces. Capitano wrote that despite his immaturity Tartaglia showed great promise and a purity rare among the Fatui. Childe was bewildered ('Why me?'): he had thought the Captain looked down on him, especially after Liyue.

Sandrone explains that Pierro needed to back a Harbinger quickly to keep the balance, and Tartaglia, though long backed by the Northland Bank, is 'not cut from the same cloth' as Pantalone. In a 7.0 session he argued that Fatui families in remote areas had 15% less Kristall than average civilian families in Snezhnograd, demanded a clear rationale for allocations, slammed the table at Pantalone's deflections, and proposed that the Fatui gather regional data under Druzhna supervision. The vote to extend Project Stuzha passed with 61 percent, a margin Childe privately thought far too close.

6.comment: Tartaglia: Project Stuzha and his conscience
6.content: When the Traveler asked why he and Sandrone were not standing up for ordinary people, Childe said that his position was close to theirs, but the Tsaritsa would never let him cast a dissenting vote. Instead he raises concerns in every session for soldiers who are 'regular folks from small towns', Morepesok among them. He trusts the Tsaritsa's long-term vision and calls the sacrifices worth it. He pointed to her eastern campaign against the blizzard-summoning beast as proof she cares for her people.

7.comment: Tartaglia: Snezhnograd, Paimon's guards and the theatre ticket
7.content: In 7.0 the Traveler first looked for him at Glupov. He then met them with Sandrone and Odette, and reluctantly told Odette that the Traveler had defeated Rosalyne in a duel before the throne, then reassured the Traveler that time had dulled the shock. With Paimon ill, he sent his most reliable soldiers to guard her. He had a subordinate pull the files on the masked troublemaker Lelek for the Traveler. Because he had to work overtime on that case, he gave them his ticket to Odette's rehearsal of 'Spirit Seeker'. Pierro later came in person and walked off with the sleeping Paimon; the guards could not stop the Director. Childe apologised for the 'misunderstanding'.

8.content: After the Tsaritsa returned triumphant, the Traveler asked Childe for an audience. He filled in the application and had the Druzhna expedite it, then met them at Zapolyarny Palace. Court etiquette has endless rules, he said, but Her Majesty dislikes excessive formality, so basic respect would do. She does not need displays of dominance; she is "inherently superior". During the session she commended him, and he privately noted that 'the old man' had his work cut out for him once the Tsaritsa ordered Pulcinella to review the House of the Hearth's list of names in a corruption probe. He left with the other ministers before the Tsaritsa's private talk with the Traveler.
